chunks: And Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji informed us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Alawi, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Malik ibn A'yun al-Juhani, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying: Every banner that is raised — or he said: comes out — before the rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him), its owner is a Taghut.
ai.seo_question: Who is considered a Taghut before the rise of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a definitive criterion for political legitimacy, declaring that any banner raised prior to the appearance of al-Qa'im belongs to a 'Taghut,' a term in Shia exegesis denoting not just tyranny but any entity claiming divine or absolute authority independent of the Imam. This hadith is central to the doctrine of the Major Occultation, providing believers with a theological basis to reject provisional caliphs and pretenders who lack the specific divine designation (Nass) of the Twelfth Imam. It underscores the continuity of Imamate authority, ensuring that pre-Qa'im rulers are viewed as temporary but ultimately illegitimate until the true Master of the Age emerges.
